limitations: This is an optional experimental Rust analyzer patch. The default vendor and public library do not apply it.

The added precheck covers direct integer DIV projections with a literal NULL numerator and a strict string-column cast chain as divisor over locally evaluable VALUES. It does not provide general Spark expression evaluation.

The 23 preceding corpora retain 153 value/type/coarse-stage differences; the new 536 observations retain 29. Widths, ANSI settings and related shapes repeat observations of the same underlying behavior.
Five older same-stage error-cause gaps, four additional empty-subquery cause gaps and four wrapped-sort diagnostics remain separate from the numeric comparator.
Spark-compatible trimming is applied only to the discarded local precheck after native evaluation fails. Ordinary runtime string-to-integer CAST compatibility is not changed by this patch.

Only eight benchmark scenarios were timed. Large VALUES inputs, the whitespace-retry path, Delta I/O and concurrent workloads were not timed separately. An unchanged physical plan is not proof of zero performance cost.
Earlier unattributed buffer-policy timing differences around 0.4%-0.7% remain outside this comparison.
